# SK8005 — `Thread.Sleep` in a test

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A test that waits for a duration passes or fails on how loaded the machine is.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Tests |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.0 |

## Why

A sleep encodes a guess about how long the thing under test takes. On a developer's idle laptop the guess holds; on a CI agent running sixteen jobs it does not, and the test fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the code. The failure is intermittent, so it is triaged as flakiness rather than as a defect, and a suite with a few of these stops being read at all. It also costs the sleep on every run, forever, including all the runs where the wait was not needed. What the test wants is a signal — a handle, a task, a callback, a polled predicate with a generous timeout — and every one of those is both faster and deterministic. ⚠ There is no fix: the replacement is a change to what the test synchronises on, which is a design decision and not an edit.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
[Fact]
public void PublishesTheEvent() {
    bus.Publish(new Ping());
    Thread.Sleep(200);
    Assert.Single(sink.Received);
}
```

Write:

```csharp
[Fact]
public void PublishesTheEvent() {
    bus.Publish(new Ping());
    Assert.True(sink.Delivered.Wait(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10)));
    Assert.Single(sink.Received);
}
```

## When it does not fire

The rule fires only where the semantic model resolves the call to `System.Threading.Thread.Sleep`, so a `Sleep` method on a user type of that name is never reported, and neither is anything at all when the symbol did not resolve. It is scoped by attribute rather than by path: the call must sit lexically inside a method carrying a recognised test attribute (`Fact`, `Theory`, `Test`, `TestCase`, `TestMethod`, `Benchmark`), which is the same set `SK3002` uses, so a sleep in a helper method a test calls, in a fixture's constructor, or anywhere in production code is outside the rule. ⚠ A `[Benchmark]` method counts as a test method for this rule because the shared helper says so; a deliberate sleep in a benchmark is the shape most likely to be reported and not wanted. The rule cannot tell a sleep that is a guess from a sleep that is the point of the test — a test of a frame limiter, a debounce, or a file watcher's coalescing window has to advance a real clock, and reports there are true and unwanted. That is what the default severity of `suggestion` and a baseline are for; a repository that wants the rule to bite promotes it in the `[**/*.Tests/**/*.cs]` section its `.editorconfig` already has.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK8005.severity`
